verifications.verifierNote: Pattern and data flow confirmed on every cited line. types.ts:36 `rating: number` is required with no 'unrated' representation; goodreads.ts:111 substitutes the sentinel `rating: Number.isFinite(rating) ? rating : 0` (Goodreads exports write 0 for unrated); goodreads.ts:74-76 `toStatus` maps shelf 'read' -> 'Finished', so read-but-unrated rows land in exactly the set StatsView averages. StatsView.tsx:20 reduces `b.rating` over all Finished books with no filter; BookCard.tsx:100 renders `{book.rating}/5` for every Finished book. Secondary claim also holds: StatsView.tsx:18-21 yields `string | number` (`.toFixed(1)` vs the literal `0`), which is why StatCard.value is widened to `string | number` at StatsView.tsx:197. One more consequence the discovery missed, which strengthens it: BookDetail.tsx:215 does `rating: newStatus === 'Finished' ? book.rating || 5 : book.rating`, so marking an unrated import Finished silently fabricates a 5-star rating out of the sentinel. Severity stays medium (wrong displayed data, no crash). Category amended: this is not two same-typed domain concepts being swapped (the branded-type definition) but a missing 'unrated' state, so discriminated-union-opportunity is the accurate bucket and keeps the report's branded-type section honest.
verifications.reachability: Import a Goodreads CSV containing read-but-unrated rows (the default for most large exports) -> the Stats headline 'Avg. Rating' is dragged toward 0 and every such book's card shows '0/5'. Marking any of them Finished from BookDetail.tsx:215 converts the sentinel into a fabricated 5.
verifications.blastRadius: 3 render/derivation sites (StatsView.tsx:20 + :93, BookCard.tsx:100, BookDetail.tsx:278-287) plus 2 writers (goodreads.ts:111, BookDetail.tsx:215).
verifications.suggestedPatch: types.ts:36 -> `rating?: number;` (absent = unrated). goodreads.ts:111 -> `...(Number.isFinite(rating) && rating > 0 ? { rating } : {})`. StatsView.tsx:18-21 -> `const rated = finished.filter((b) => (b.rating ?? 0) > 0); const avgRating = rated.length ? (rated.reduce((a, b) => a + (b.rating ?? 0), 0) / rated.length).toFixed(1) : '--';` (always a string, so StatCard.value narrows to `string`). BookCard.tsx:100 -> render the badge only when rating is set. Risk: making `rating` optional touches every Book literal (repo create calls, test fixtures) - mechanical, but compile-wide.
verifications.amendedDescription: Same defect as filed, re-categorised. `Book.rating: number` has no representation for 'unrated', so goodreads.ts:111 encodes absence as the sentinel 0; StatsView.tsx:20 averages it in and reports a false 'Avg. Rating' after any Goodreads import, BookCard.tsx:100 prints an authoritative '0/5', and BookDetail.tsx:215 (`book.rating || 5`) turns the sentinel into an invented 5-star rating when the book is marked Finished. The fix is an explicit absent state (optional field or tagged rating), not a brand.

verifications.verifierNote: The code is exactly as described: ConfirmDialog.tsx:18-19 holds the pending confirm in two independent nullable slots and confirm() at :21-26 assigns `resolverRef.current = resolve` unconditionally, so a second pending confirm would strand the first promise. What does NOT hold is reachability. ConfirmProvider renders a single Dialog (:39-44) and Dialog.tsx:21-29 mounts a `fixed inset-0 z-50` backdrop only while open, whose onClick settles the pending confirm with false. All three consumers call confirm() as the first statement of a click/FileReader handler (ProfilePage.tsx:16, BookDetailPage.tsx:28, ProfileView.tsx:125), so React flushes the discrete-event update and mounts the backdrop before a second click can reach any trigger. I could not construct a path in the current app where two confirms are pending simultaneously. The provider-unmount leak is real but costs only a retained closure whose continuation is `if (!confirmed) return`. Amended down to low: genuine latent modelling defect, no current incident path.
verifications.reachability: Not reachable today - the single full-screen modal makes confirmation exclusive by construction. Re-opens the moment anyone adds a non-blocking confirm surface (inline/toast-style), a second ConfirmProvider, or a programmatic confirm not driven by a user click.
verifications.blastRadius: 3 non-test consumers (ProfileView.tsx:125 backup import, ProfilePage.tsx:16 delete-whole-library, BookDetailPage.tsx:28 delete-book).
verifications.suggestedPatch: Collapse the two slots into one tagged state: `type Pending = { status: 'idle' } | { status: 'pending'; options: ConfirmOptions; resolve: (v: boolean) => void }`, and inside the Promise executor do `setPending((prev) => { if (prev.status === 'pending') prev.resolve(false); return { status: 'pending', options: next, resolve }; })`. Render the Dialog body only when pending, which deletes the five `?.`/`?? ''` fallbacks at :41/45/51/56/61. Risk: `resolve` must be captured inside `new Promise`, so the state update has to happen in the executor rather than before it.
verifications.amendedDescription: ConfirmDialog holds one logical pending-confirm as two unrelated nullable slots (options state at :18, resolver ref at :19), and confirm() at :24 overwrites any in-flight resolver, so the invariant 'open implies options implies resolver' is unencoded and violable. No current call path can produce two pending confirms - the provider's single full-screen modal backdrop (Dialog.tsx:24-29) makes confirmation exclusive - so this is latent refactor risk, not a live hang. Fixing it also removes the five `?.`/`?? ''` fallbacks the current shape forces in the JSX.

verifications.verifierNote: Pattern confirmed at useFocusTrap.ts:18 - `querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(FOCUSABLE)` is an unchecked generic assertion; the compiler never parses the selector at :5. Half the discovery rationale is wrong: grep for `<a ` across src/**/*.tsx returns ZERO inline anchors and there is no `tabIndex` attribute anywhere in the app, so no SVG node can match `a[href]` or `[tabindex]` and the SVGAElement scenario is unreachable. The visibility half is real, and I found the concrete site: AddBookModal.tsx:229-235 renders `<input type="file" className="hidden">` (display:none) inside a Dialog, and in upload mode with no file chosen the submit button at :262-266 is `disabled` and therefore excluded by `button:not([disabled])`. The hidden input is then the LAST entry in `focusable()`, so `last` at useFocusTrap.ts:48 can never equal `document.activeElement`, the forward-Tab wrap at :54-57 never fires, and Tab escapes the aria-modal dialog - the exact guarantee the hook exists to provide. Severity stays medium (accessibility degradation, no crash). The two `!` at :47-48 are guarded by `if (items.length === 0) return;` at :45, consistent with earlier batches.

verifications.verifierNote: Confirmed at LibraryPage.tsx:35: `const parsed = JSON.parse(cached) as { at: number; items: Recommendation[] };` - a bare assertion over localStorage, with the try/catch at :34-41 covering only JSON.parse, so a syntactically valid but wrong-shaped value passes and the self-healing removeItem at :40 never runs. The value flows to setRecommendations(:37) -> RecommendationCarousel `recommendations.map` (:79) and `rec.coverUrl`/`rec.title`/`rec.author` (:91-104). Two refinements from tracing the producer. (a) The app itself cannot write a non-array `items`: recommend.ts:34-39 always returns the result of `.map`, and a non-array `data.recommendations` throws inside recommend.ts's own try and is converted by toAiError - so the `items:"abc"` crash needs a foreign same-origin writer, devtools, or a future `Recommendation` shape change leaving 24h of stale caches. (b) The field-level variant IS live today: recommend.ts:35-36 spreads model output verbatim (`...rec`), so a response missing `title` yields `key={undefined}` and a missing `description` renders blank, then gets cached. Worth adding: the TTL test at :36 is `Date.now() - parsed.at < RECS_TTL_MS`, which is also true for any FUTURE `at`, so a poisoned entry with a forward timestamp never expires. Medium is right - localStorage ingress, no app-writable crash path today.

verifications.verifierNote: Confirmed and under-graded. types.ts:89 declares `correctAnswerIndex: number` with nothing relating it to `options.length`; schemas.ts:69-72 declares it as a bare `Type.NUMBER` whose '0-3' constraint lives only in a `description` string, while genai.d.ts exposes `minimum?` (:12073) and `maximum?` (:12065) unused; the `options` array's '4 answers' constraint at schemas.ts:64-68 is likewise description-only. ReviewPage.tsx:76 and :94 compare indices with no bounds check, and the finding is precise about the consequence: ReviewPage never does `options[correctAnswerIndex]`, so there is no crash - instead `showCorrect` is false for every option and `isCorrect` is false for every possible selection, so the card is permanently unanswerable-correctly, the explanation at :120 describes an answer not on screen, and the card stays in rotation being graded wrong forever. Amending UP to high: this is a known-runtime-data ingress (Gemini JSON -> IndexedDB -> typed code) with no validation at any layer, which the spec's high band names explicitly, and the specific corruption is a well-known model behaviour (1-based indices - returning 4 for a 4-option array is off-by-one and silently out of range). Silent, permanent, and it degrades rather than blocks, so it will not get reported by users.

verifications.verifierNote: The facts check out: useTheme.test.tsx:27-39 installs a hand-built matchMedia via `vi.stubGlobal`, whose value parameter is `unknown`, so nothing checks the stub against `MediaQueryList`; `addEventListener: vi.fn()` (:32) records calls and never invokes the handler, so useTheme.ts:22-24 (`onChange` and the removeEventListener cleanup) is never exercised; both system tests (:61-71) set the preference before mount and assert the initial resolution from `useState(systemPrefersDark)` at useTheme.ts:17; and useTheme.ts:23-24's optional call (`query.addEventListener?.(...)`) means a stub - or a browser - lacking the method silently stops subscribing with every test still green. But the severity and the category are both off. The `unknown` belongs to Vitest's own stubGlobal signature, not to this codebase, and is genuinely correct for an API that can stub anything - the spec's own guidance is to accept type looseness at platform/library shims rather than file it. The stub is not a lying fixture either: it has every MediaQueryList member, just inert. What is left is a test-coverage gap whose worst outcome is that a live OS theme switch stops re-theming until reload - cosmetic. Amended to low.

verifications.amendedDescription: useTheme.test.tsx:27-39 installs a hand-built matchMedia through `vi.stubGlobal`, which accepts `unknown`, so the stub is never checked against `MediaQueryList` and could drift silently. Its `addEventListener` (:32) never invokes the handler, so useTheme.ts:22-24 - the live system-theme subscription and its cleanup - is dead code from this suite's point of view, and useTheme.ts:23's optional call means a missing method would go unnoticed in production too. Both 'system' tests (:61-71) only assert the initial resolution from useTheme.ts:17. Hygiene plus a coverage gap: the `unknown` is Vitest's API rather than a codebase choice, and the worst outcome is that a live OS theme switch fails to re-theme until reload.

verifications.verifierNote: Confirmed end to end. chat.ts:32 coalesces `chunk.text ?? ''` and :35 returns the accumulated string, so a completion that yields no text at all (safety block on the reply, empty candidate list, immediately-truncated stream) completes the loop without throwing and returns `''`; `Promise<string>` at :27 cannot express the difference, so callers get no compiler-visible reason to handle it. On the consumer side ChatModal.tsx:59 pushes the placeholder `{ role: 'model', text: '' }`, :61 awaits the stream, `onChunk` is never invoked so the placeholder is never filled, and the recovery block at :69-79 is inside a `catch` that never fires on this path - while the condition it uses, `entry.text === ''` at :74, describes exactly the state produced here. The user is left with a permanently blank assistant bubble, no toast, no retry affordance. The suggested shape is supported: errors.ts:1-9 already defines the `'safety'` kind and errors.ts:33 its user-facing copy. Medium is right - one call site, UI dead-end, no crash or data loss.
verifications.reachability: Ask a question in the book chat that Gemini declines to answer (safety/recitation finish reason with no text parts): the assistant bubble appears and stays empty forever.

verifications.suggestedPatch: chat.ts:35 -> `if (text === '') throw new AiError('safety', MESSAGES-backed copy); return text;` - concretely `if (!text) throw new AiError('safety', 'Gemini blocked this request under its safety filters. Try a different book or wording.');` (import AiError from './errors'). ChatModal's existing catch at :69-79 then fills the empty placeholder with the message, so no consumer change is needed. Risk: a legitimate empty reply (model chooses silence) would now surface as an error - acceptable, since a blank bubble is not a usable outcome either.

verifications.verifierNote: Confirmed, and I traced the throw by hand against the current source. errors.ts:39-42 `statusOf` does `const status = (error as { status?: unknown }).status;` with no null guard, and toAiError(undefined) flows: :46 not an AiError -> :48 `message = String(undefined)` = 'undefined' -> :53/:54 no 'quota'/'safety'/'blocked' match -> :55 not SyntaxError -> :56 not TypeError -> :57 else -> :58 `statusOf(undefined)` -> :40 throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'status')`. Identical for null. Strings and numbers are safe (property access boxes the primitive), so it is exactly the two nullish values that break. errors.test.ts contains no such fixture: :4-6 `apiError` builds a real Error, and every other case is `new MissingKeyError()` / `new TypeError` (:34) / `new SyntaxError` (:38) / apiError (:14-23, :25-31, :41-47). The `as { status?: unknown }` is the lie - it asserts objecthood on a parameter declared `unknown`. This is a genuine bug in the app's universal error normaliser (every AI entry point does `catch (error) { throw toAiError(error) }`), so it belongs in the report's 'Bugs discovered' section. Medium is right: the fix is one line, but the triggering values (`throw undefined`, `Promise.reject()` with no argument) are rare in practice, so I would not raise it to high without a demonstrated producer.

I could not find a producer in the SDK or app code, so the crash is latent - but the function's declared parameter type promises to handle it.

verifications.suggestedPatch: errors.ts:39-42 -> `function statusOf(error: unknown): number | undefined { if (typeof error !== 'object' || error === null) return undefined; const status = (error as { status?: unknown }).status; return typeof status === 'number' ? status : undefined; }` and add two table cases to errors.test.ts: `it.each([[undefined], [null], ['boom'], [42]])('normalises %p to an AiError', (v) => expect(toAiError(v)).toBeInstanceOf(AiError))`. Risk: none - strictly widens the accepted input set.

verifications.verifierNote: The mechanics are exactly as described - prompts.ts:39-42 interpolates `booksList` raw, recommend.ts:20-22 builds it from unescaped, uncapped `b.title` / `b.author` / `b.category`, and the same raw interpolation occurs at prompts.ts:24, :45, :56 and :79, several of which also embed prior model output (`summary.summary`, `summary.keyInsights`). The verified negative is accurate too: prompts.ts has no assertions, no `!`, and :79's `type: 'short' | 'long'` is a proper literal union. But medium under boundary-without-validation overstates it on two counts. (1) Category: nothing external is being TYPED here - data flows OUT of typed code into a string, so no type is claiming correctness the runtime cannot deliver. The argument the finding actually makes ('a string that controls a request's output contract is interchangeable with a display string') is a branded-type argument, and the spec explicitly warns those belong only where the foot-gun cost is real. (2) Cost: BookSum is local-first with no server, no accounts and no other party's data - the 'attacker' supplies their own CSV and their own API key, so a crafted title can only steer the model into returning junk to the user who wrote it, and there is no exfiltration channel. The real defence the finding itself names - validating at the parse site - is already filed separately (the unvalidated Recommendation cast). Amended to low with the category corrected.
verifications.reachability: A user imports a Goodreads CSV whose title field contains instructions, then refreshes recommendations. The steered response reaches the consumer as a typed `Recommendation[]`. No privilege boundary is crossed - the only affected party is the author of the input.
verifications.blastRadius: 5 prompt builders (prompts.ts:24, :39, :45, :56, :79) fed by 1 unescaped join (recommend.ts:20-22).
verifications.suggestedPatch: Cheapest effective step, in recommend.ts:20-22 rather than in every builder: `const clean = (s: string) => s.replace(/[\r\n]+/g, ' ').slice(0, 120); const booksList = userBooks.slice(0, 100).map((b) => `"${clean(b.title)}" by ${clean(b.author)} (${clean(b.category)})`).join(', ');`. The slice(0, 100) also caps prompt size for large imported libraries, which is the more likely real-world problem. Risk: truncation changes recommendation quality for very long titles - acceptable; keep the parse-site validation as the actual defence.
verifications.amendedDescription: recommend.ts:20-22 builds the prompt fragment from unescaped, uncapped user-imported `title`/`author`/`category`, and prompts.ts:39-42 interpolates it directly above the sentence that defines the requested output shape; the same raw interpolation appears at prompts.ts:24, :45, :56 and :79. `Book.title` etc. are plain `string` (types.ts:31-33), with no distinction between 'display text' and 'text that steers a request contract'. In a local-first, single-user, no-server app this crosses no privilege boundary - the only party who can inject is the party who receives the output - so treat it as hygiene (escape newlines, cap length, cap the number of books to bound prompt size) and keep validation at the parse site as the real defence.

verifications.verifierNote: All four layers verified. schemas.ts:8 `category: { type: Type.STRING }` has no enum, while genai.d.ts:12051 exposes `enum?: string[]` unused. The allowed values exist only as prose at prompts.ts:12. types.ts:33 declares `category: string`. And types.ts:6-15's `Category` enum is genuinely dead - a repo-wide grep for `Category` returns only that declaration, JSX label text (BookDetail.tsx:321, StatsView.tsx:133/138), a comment and unrelated identifiers (`activeCategory`, `categoryMap`); nothing imports it. summarize.ts:26 `category: data.category || 'Other'` confirms the finding's sharpest point: the fallback fires on empty/undefined only, never on a non-empty wrong string, so 'Self-Help' is accepted and persisted verbatim. LibraryPage.tsx:65 then builds the filter chips from `new Set(books.map((b) => b.category))`, so near-duplicate one-book categories accrete in the filter bar and StatsView.tsx:23-28's breakdown fragments. Medium is right: silent data-quality drift, no crash, and the codebase already contains the enum that documents the invariant nothing enforces.

verifications.verifierNote: Confirmed against source. schemas.ts:13-21 declares readingTimeMinutes and rating as bare `Type.NUMBER` with the range only in a `description`, while genai.d.ts:12073 `minimum?` and :12065 `maximum?` sit unused. types.ts:36/47 are unbranded `number`. summarize.ts:28-29 applies `rating: data.rating ?? 0` and `readingTimeMinutes: data.readingTimeMinutes ?? 5` - nullish coalescing only, so 8.7, -3 and 100000 all pass through. The two paths are as claimed: AddBookModal.tsx:74 overwrites `rating` with the user's slider value, but LibraryPage.tsx:91-94 (add-from-recommendation) spreads `...book` straight into addBook, persisting the model's number verbatim with no user override. Display consequences verified: BookCard.tsx:100 renders `{book.rating}/5` -> '8.7/5'; BookDetail.tsx:278/282 light every star via `num <= Math.round(book.rating)` and :287 prints the raw value; StatsView.tsx:20 folds it into the average forever. Medium is right - no crash, permanently wrong displayed data with no correction path on the recommendation route. Note this compounds F061: the same average is polluted from both ends (Goodreads sentinel 0s and unclamped model ratings).

verifications.suggestedPatch: schemas.ts:18-21 -> add `minimum: 1, maximum: 5`; :13-17 -> add `minimum: 1, maximum: 600`. Then clamp in summarize.ts's toGenerated, which already normalises every other field: `const clamp = (n: number | undefined, lo: number, hi: number, dflt: number) => (typeof n === 'number' && Number.isFinite(n) ? Math.min(hi, Math.max(lo, Math.round(n))) : dflt);` used as `rating: clamp(data.rating, 1, 5, 0)` and `readingTimeMinutes: clamp(data.readingTimeMinutes, 1, 600, 5)`. Risk: rounding changes existing snapshot expectations in summarize tests; existing out-of-range records are not repaired by this and would need a migration if any exist.
